sanskrit: so 'rjunena parāmṛṣṭaḥ paryadevayad ārtavat bahulaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ caiva virāṭasya sutas tadā
english: Seized by Arjuna, the son of Virāṭa lamented piteously then, weeping much and pitifully.

sanskrit: śātakumbhasya śuddhasya śataṃ niṣkān dadāmi te maṇīn aṣṭau ca vaiḍūryān hemabaddhān mahāprabhān
english: "I will give you a hundred niṣkas of pure refined gold, and eight great-lustred beryl gems set in gold.

sanskrit: hemadaṇḍapraticchannaṃ rathaṃ yuktaṃ ca suvrajaiḥ mattāṃś ca daśa mātaṅgān muñca māṃ tvaṃ bṛhannaḍe
english: A chariot fitted with gold staffs and harnessed with fine horses, and ten maddened elephants — release me, O Bṛhannaḍā!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evamādīni vākyāni vilapantam acetasam prahasya puruṣavyāghro rathasyāntikam ānayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Laughing at these and such words of the senseless, lamenting one, the tiger among men brought the chariot near.

sanskrit: athainam abravīt pārtho bhayārtaṃ naṣṭacetasam yadi notsahase yoddhuṃ śatrubhiḥ śatrukarśana ehi me tvaṃ hayān yaccha yudhyamānasya śatrubhiḥ
english: Then Pārtha spoke to him who was overcome with fear and had lost his wits: "If you dare not fight the enemies, O tormentor of foes, come and hold the horses for me while I engage the enemies in battle."

sanskrit: prayāhy etad rathānīkaṃ madbāhubalarakṣitaḥ apradhṛṣyatamaṃ ghoraṃ guptaṃ vīrair mahārathaiḥ
english: "Advance toward that army of chariots, protected by the strength of my arms — that terrible, most formidable force guarded by great warriors and mighty chariot-fighters."

sanskrit: mā bhais tvaṃ rājaputrāgrya kṣatriyo 'si paraṃtapa ahaṃ vai kurubhir yotsyāmy avajeṣyāmi te paśūn
english: "Fear not, O foremost of princes! You are a kṣatriya, O scorcher of foes. I shall fight the Kurus and recover your cattle."

sanskrit: praviśyaitad rathānīkam apradhṛṣyaṃ durāsadam yantā bhūs tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha yotsye 'haṃ kurubhiḥ saha
english: "Enter this chariot army that is unassailable and hard to approach; be the charioteer, O best of men, while I fight with the Kurus."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇo bībhatsur vairāṭim aparājitaḥ samāśvāsya muhūrtaṃ tam uttaraṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Speaking thus, the invincible Bībhatsu, O bull of the Bhārata line, for a moment comforted that prince Uttara, the son of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ viceṣṭantam akāmaṃ bhayapīḍitam ratham āropayām āsa pārthaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, the foremost of warriors, mounted him — unwilling and oppressed with fear and struggling — onto the chariot.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ dṛṣṭvā klībaveṣeṇa rathasthaṃ narapuṃgavam śamīm abhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ ratham āropya cottaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing that bull among men, clad in eunuch's garb, standing on the chariot with Uttara now mounted, heading toward the śamī tree —

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇamukhās tatra kurūṇāṃ rathasattamāḥ vitrastamanasaḥ sarve dhanaṃjayakṛtād bhayāt
english: — the foremost chariot warriors of the Kurus, led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, were all struck with terror at the fear inspired by Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tān avekṣya hatotsāhān utpātān api cādbhutān guruḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho bhāradvājo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Observing them dispirited and beholding also the portentous omens, the preceptor Bhāradvāja, foremost of weapon-bearers, addressed them.

sanskrit: calāś ca vātāḥ saṃvānti rūkṣāḥ paruṣaniḥsvanāḥ bhasmavarṇaprakāśena tamasā saṃvṛtaṃ nabhaḥ
english: "Harsh winds blow restlessly with rough, harsh sounds; the sky is covered with darkness of an ashen hue.

sanskrit: rūkṣavarṇāś ca jaladā dṛśyante 'dbhutadarśanāḥ niḥsaranti ca kośebhyaḥ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Clouds of grim colour appear with wondrous appearance; and various weapons are issuing out of their sheaths by themselves.

sanskrit: śivāś ca vinadanty etā dīptāyāṃ diśi dāruṇāḥ hayāś cāśrūṇi muñcanti dhvajāḥ kampanty akampitāḥ
english: Terrible jackals howl in the blazing quarter; horses shed tears and standards tremble though there is no wind.

sanskrit: yādṛśāny atra rūpāṇi saṃdṛśyante bahūny api yattā bhavantas tiṣṭhantu syād yuddhaṃ samupasthitam
english: Given the many signs and forms seen here, let all of you stand alert — battle seems to be at hand.

sanskrit: rakṣadhvam api cātmānaṃ vyūhadhvaṃ vāhinīm api vaiśasaṃ ca pratīkṣadhvaṃ rakṣadhvaṃ cāpi godhanam
english: Guard yourselves; array the army in battle-formation; be ready for slaughter; and protect the cattle as well.

sanskrit: eṣa vīro maheṣvāsaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ āgataḥ klībaveṣeṇa pārtho nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: This great bowman, the best of all weapon-bearers, who has come in the disguise of a eunuch — he is Pārtha; there is no doubt in this.

sanskrit: sa eṣa pārtho vikrāntaḥ savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ nāyuddhena nivarteta sarvair api marudgaṇaiḥ
english: This very Pārtha, valiant Savyasācī, the scorcher of foes — he would not turn back from battle even against all the hosts of the Maruts.

sanskrit: kleśitaś ca vane śūro vāsavena ca śikṣitaḥ amarṣavaśam āpanno yotsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Afflicted in the forest, trained by Vāsava himself, this hero — overcome by righteous wrath — will fight. Of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: nehāsya pratiyoddhāram ahaṃ paśyāmi kauravāḥ mahādevo 'pi pārthena śrūyate yudhi toṣitaḥ
english: I see no opponent worthy of him here, O Kauravas. Even Mahādeva, it is heard, was pleased with Pārtha in battle.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca sadā bhavān phalgunasya guṇair asmān vikatthase na cārjunaḥ kalā pūrṇā mama duryodhanasya vā
english: Karṇa said: "You always boast to us of Phalguna's virtues; yet Arjuna is not a full part equal to me or to Duryodhana."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca yady eṣa pārtho rādheya kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ bhaven mama jñātāḥ punaś cariṣyanti dvādaśānyān hi vatsarān
english: Duryodhana said: "If this is indeed Pārtha, O son of Rādhā, my purpose would be accomplished — our kinsmen would have to spend another twelve years in exile."

sanskrit: athaiṣa kaś cid evānyaḥ klībaveṣeṇa mānavaḥ śarair enaṃ suniśitaiḥ pātayiṣyāmi bhūtale
english: "Or if this is merely some other man dressed as a eunuch, I shall strike him down to the ground with my well-sharpened arrows."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin bruvati tad vākyaṃ dhārtarāṣṭre paraṃtape bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpo drauṇiḥ pauruṣaṃ tad apūjayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that scorcher of foes, spoke those words, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa applauded that sentiment of valor.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tāṃ śamīm upasaṃgamya pārtho vairāṭim abravīt sukumāraṃ samājñātaṃ saṃgrāme nātikovidam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Approaching that śamī tree, Pārtha addressed the son of Virāṭa — that delicate youth of noble birth, not greatly skilled in battle.

sanskrit: samādiṣṭo mayā kṣipraṃ dhanūṃṣy avaharottara nemāni hi tvadīyāni soḍhuṃ śakṣyanti me balam
english: "As I have commanded you, quickly bring down the bows from this tree, Uttara — for these own bows of yours cannot bear my strength."

sanskrit: bhāraṃ vāpi guruṃ hartuṃ kuñjaraṃ vā pramarditum mama vā bāhuvikṣepaṃ śatrūn iha vijeṣyataḥ
english: "They could not bear the heavy weight, nor endure an elephant's crushing force, nor the sweeping pull of my arms as I conquer the enemies here."

sanskrit: tasmād bhūmiṃjayāroha śamīm etāṃ palāśinīm asyāṃ hi pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ dhanūṃṣi nihitāny uta
english: "Therefore, O Bhūmiṃjaya, climb this leafy śamī tree — for in it the bows of the sons of Pāṇḍu are deposited."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya bhīmasya bībhatsor yamayos tathā dhvajāḥ śarāś ca śūrāṇāṃ divyāni kavacāni ca
english: "The standards, arrows and divine armour of those heroes — of Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Bībhatsu, and the twin sons of Mādrī — are all there."

sanskrit: atra caitan mahāvīryaṃ dhanuḥ pārthasya gāṇḍivam ekaṃ śatasahasreṇa saṃmitaṃ rāṣṭravardhanam
english: "Here too is this Gāṇḍīva, Pārtha's bow of great power, equal in worth to a hundred thousand bows — the increaser of the kingdom."

sanskrit: vyāyāmasaham atyarthaṃ tṛṇarājasamaṃ mahat sarvāyudhamahāmātraṃ śatrusaṃbādhakārakam
english: "Exceedingly capable of enduring great exertion, great as the king of grasses, supreme among all weapons, the afflicting cause of enemies."

sanskrit: suvarṇavikṛtaṃ divyaṃ ślakṣṇam āyatam avraṇam alaṃ bhāraṃ guruṃ voḍhuṃ dāruṇaṃ cārudarśanam tādṛśāny eva sarvāṇi balavanti dṛḍhāni ca
english: "Adorned with gold, divine, smooth, long, without blemish, fully capable of bearing great weight, terrible yet beautiful to behold — and all the others are equally powerful and sturdy."

sanskrit: uttara uvāca asmin vṛkṣe kilodbaddhaṃ śarīram iti naḥ śrutam tad ahaṃ rājaputraḥ san spṛśeyaṃ pāṇinā katham
english: Uttara said: "We have heard that a corpse is bound in this tree. How then can I, being a prince, touch it with my hand?"

sanskrit: naivaṃvidhaṃ mayā yuktam ālabdhuṃ kṣatrayoninā mahatā rājaputreṇa mantrayajñavidā satā
english: "It is not proper for me, born of kṣatriya lineage, a great prince, knower of mantras and sacrifices and of virtuous character, to touch such a thing."

sanskrit: spṛṣṭavantaṃ śarīraṃ māṃ śavavāham ivāśucim kathaṃ vā vyavahāryaṃ vai kurvīthās tvaṃ bṛhannaḍe
english: "Having touched a corpse, impure as a corpse-carrier, how could you then deal with me as with a pure person, O Bṛhannaḍā?"

sanskrit: bṛhannaḍovāca vyavahāryaś ca rājendra śuciś caiva bhaviṣyasi dhanūṃṣy etāni mā bhais tvaṃ śarīraṃ nātra vidyate
english: Bṛhannaḍā said: "You will remain fit for dealings with others and pure indeed, O lord of kings. Fear not these bows — there is no corpse here."

sanskrit: dāyādaṃ matsyarājasya kule jātaṃ manasvinam kathaṃ tvā ninditaṃ karma kārayeyaṃ nṛpātmaja
english: "How could I make you, the heir and son born in the lineage of the king of the Matsyas, a man of noble spirit, do a censurable act, O son of a king?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa pārthena rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī āruroha śamīvṛkṣaṃ vairāṭir avaśas tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Pārtha, the earring-adorned son of Virāṭa leapt from the chariot and unwillingly climbed the śamī tree.

sanskrit: tam anvaśāsac chatrughno rathe tiṣṭhan dhanaṃjayaḥ pariveṣṭanam eteṣāṃ kṣipraṃ caiva vyapānuda
english: Standing on the chariot, Dhanaṃjaya instructed him and quickly undid the coverings of those weapons.

sanskrit: tathā saṃnahanāny eṣāṃ parimucya samantataḥ apaśyad gāṇḍivaṃ tatra caturbhir aparaiḥ saha
english: Loosening all their fastenings on every side likewise, he saw the Gāṇḍīva there together with four other bows.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vimucyamānānāṃ dhanuṣām arkavarcasām viniśceruḥ prabhā divyā grahāṇām udayeṣv iva
english: As those bows bright as the sun were being loosened, their divine radiance blazed forth like the rising of planets.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ rūpam ālokya bhoginām iva jṛmbhatām hṛṣṭaromā bhayodvignaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: Beholding their forms stretching out like serpents uncoiling, his hair stood erect and in an instant he became stricken with fear.

sanskrit: saṃspṛśya tāni cāpāni bhānumanti bṛhanti ca vairāṭir arjunaṃ rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having touched those radiant and great bows, the son of Virāṭa spoke these words to Arjuna, O king.

sanskrit: uttara uvāca bindavo jātarūpasya śataṃ yasmin nipātitāḥ sahasrakoṭi sauvarṇāḥ kasyaitad dhanur uttamam
english: Uttara said: "On which a hundred drops of refined gold have been set, and thousands of golden fittings — whose is this excellent bow?"

sanskrit: vāraṇā yasya sauvarṇāḥ pṛṣṭhe bhāsanti daṃśitāḥ supārśvaṃ sugrahaṃ caiva kasyaitad dhanuruttamam
english: "On whose back golden elephants shine, armour-clad, with fine sides and easy to grip — whose is this excellent bow?"

sanskrit: tapanīyasya śuddhasya ṣaṣṭir yasyendragopakāḥ pṛṣṭhe vibhaktāḥ śobhante kasyaitad dhanur uttamam
english: "On whose back sixty indragopaka insects of pure refined gold are arranged and gleam — whose is this excellent bow?"

sanskrit: sūryā yatra ca sauvarṇās trayo bhāsanti daṃśitāḥ tejasā prajvalanto hi kasyaitad dhanur uttamam
english: "On which three golden suns blaze, armour-clad, blazing with splendour — whose is this excellent bow?"

sanskrit: śālabhā yatra sauvarṇās tapanīyavicitritāḥ suvarṇamaṇicitraṃ ca kasyaitad dhanur uttamam
english: "On which golden locusts variegated in refined gold are set, and which is adorned with gold and gems — whose is this excellent bow?"

sanskrit: ime ca kasya nārācāḥ sahasrā lomavāhinaḥ samantāt kaladhautāgrā upāsaṅge hiraṇmaye
english: "And whose are these thousands of iron arrows with quill-like flights, tipped all around with refined silver, in a golden quiver?"

sanskrit: vipāṭhāḥ pṛthavaḥ kasya gārdhrapatrāḥ śilāśitāḥ hāridravarṇāḥ sunasāḥ pītāḥ sarvāyasāḥ śarāḥ
english: "Whose are these broad, thick arrows with vulture feathers, sharpened on stone, turmeric-coloured, well-tipped, yellow, and wholly iron?"

sanskrit: kasyāyam asitāvāpaḥ pañcaśārdūlalakṣaṇaḥ varāhakarṇavyāmiśraḥ śarān dhārayate daśa
english: "Whose is this dark-inlaid quiver bearing the mark of five tigers, mixed with boar-ear feathered arrows, holding ten shafts?"

sanskrit: kasyeme pṛthavo dīrghāḥ sarvapāraśavāḥ śarāḥ śatāni sapta tiṣṭhanti nārācā rudhirāśanāḥ
english: "Whose are these broad, long, entirely iron arrows — seven hundred nārāca shafts that drink blood standing ready?"

sanskrit: kasyeme śukapatrābhaiḥ pūrvair ardhaiḥ suvāsasaḥ uttarair āyasaiḥ pītair hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: "Whose are these arrows — their forward halves beautifully feathered like parrot wings, their rear halves yellow iron with golden nocks, sharpened on stone?"

sanskrit: kasyāyaṃ sāyako dīrghaḥ śilīpṛṣṭhaḥ śilīmukhaḥ vaiyāghrakośe nihito hemacitratsarur mahān
english: "Whose is this long arrow, smooth-backed and sharp-pointed, placed in a tiger-skin sheath, with a large handle adorned in gold?"

sanskrit: suphalaś citrakośaś ca kiṅkiṇīsāyako mahān kasya hematsarur divyaḥ khaḍgaḥ paramanirvraṇaḥ
english: "Whose is this sword with a fine blade, in a decorated sheath, a great arrow hung with small bells, with a divine golden hilt, completely unblemished?"

sanskrit: kasyāyaṃ vimalaḥ khaḍgo gavye kośe samarpitaḥ hematsarur anādhṛṣyo naiṣadhyo bhārasādhanaḥ
english: "Whose is this spotless sword placed in a cow-hide sheath, with a golden hilt, irresistible — the sword of Naiṣadha, capable of bearing great weight?"

sanskrit: kasya pāñcanakhe kośe sāyako hemavigrahaḥ pramāṇarūpasaṃpannaḥ pīta ākāśasaṃnibhaḥ
english: "Whose arrow in a five-nailed sheath has a golden form, endowed with perfect measure and appearance, yellow and resembling the sky?"

sanskrit: kasya hemamaye kośe sutapte pāvakaprabhe nistriṃśo 'yaṃ guruḥ pītaḥ saikyaḥ paramanirvraṇaḥ
english: "Whose is this heavy, yellow, polished, entirely unblemished sword — a nistriṃśa blade in a golden sheath, well-heated and blazing like fire?"

sanskrit: nirdiśasva yathātattvaṃ mayā pṛṣṭā bṛhannaḍe vismayo me paro jāto dṛṣṭvā sarvam idaṃ mahat
english: "Tell me truthfully as I ask you, O Bṛhannaḍā — great wonder has arisen in me upon seeing all these magnificent things."

sanskrit: bṛhannaḍovāca yan māṃ pūrvam ihāpṛcchaḥ śatrusenānibarhaṇam gāṇḍīvam etat pārthasya lokeṣu viditaṃ dhanuḥ
english: Bṛhannaḍā said: "What you first asked me about — the destroyer of enemy armies — this is Gāṇḍīva, Pārtha's bow, renowned throughout the worlds."

sanskrit: sarvāyudhamahāmātraṃ śātakumbhapariṣkṛtam etat tad arjunasyāsīd gāṇḍīvaṃ paramāyudham
english: "This supreme weapon of all arms, adorned with refined gold — this is Arjuna's Gāṇḍīva, the paramount weapon."

sanskrit: yat tac chatasahasreṇa saṃmitaṃ rāṣṭravardhanam yena devān manuṣyāṃś ca pārtho viṣahate mṛdhe
english: "That which is equal in worth to a hundred thousand bows, the increaser of the kingdom — with this Pārtha withstands both gods and men in battle."

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvaiḥ pūjitaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ etad varṣasahasraṃ tu brahmā pūrvam adhārayat
english: "Honoured by gods, dānavas and gandharvas through eternal ages — Brahmā first held this bow for a thousand years."

sanskrit: tato 'nantaram evātha prajāpatir adhārayat trīṇi pañcaśataṃ caiva śakro 'śīti ca pañca ca
english: "After him, Prajāpati held it; then three hundred and five hundred years; and Śakra held it for eighty-five years."

sanskrit: somaḥ pañcaśataṃ rājā tathaiva varuṇaḥ śatam pārthaḥ pañca ca ṣaṣṭiṃ ca varṣāṇi śvetavāhanaḥ
english: "King Soma held it for five hundred years; likewise Varuṇa for a hundred; and Pārtha the white-horsed one has held it for sixty-five years."

sanskrit: mahāvīryaṃ mahad divyam etat tad dhanur uttamam pūjitaṃ suramartyeṣu bibharti paramaṃ vapuḥ
english: "Of great power, great, divine — this supreme bow, honoured among gods and mortals, bears its paramount form."

sanskrit: supārśvaṃ bhīmasenasya jātarūpagrahaṃ dhanuḥ yena pārtho 'jayat kṛtsnāṃ diśaṃ prācīṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: "The bow with fine sides and a gold grip — that is Bhīmasena's, with which Pārtha the scorcher of foes conquered the entire eastern quarter."

sanskrit: indragopakacitraṃ ca yad etac cāruvigraham rājño yudhiṣṭhirasyaitad vairāṭe dhanur uttamam
english: "And this one, beautifully formed and adorned with indragopaka insects — this is the excellent bow of King Yudhiṣṭhira, O son of Virāṭa."

sanskrit: sūryā yasmiṃs tu sauvarṇāḥ prabhāsante prabhāsinaḥ tejasā prajvalanto vai nakulasyaitad āyudham
english: "On which golden suns shine brilliantly, blazing with splendour — this is Nakula's weapon."

sanskrit: śalabhā yatra sauvarṇās tapanīyavicitritāḥ etan mādrīsutasyāpi sahadevasya kārmukam
english: "On which golden locusts variegated in refined gold are set — this is the bow of the son of Mādrī, Sahadeva."

sanskrit: ye tv ime kṣurasaṃkāśāḥ sahasrā lomavāhinaḥ ete 'rjunasya vairāṭe śarāḥ sarpaviṣopamāḥ
english: "And these thousands of razor-like arrows with quill feathers — these are Arjuna's arrows in the land of Virāṭa, equal in venom to serpents."

sanskrit: ete jvalantaḥ saṃgrāme tejasā śīghragāminaḥ bhavanti vīrasyākṣayyā vyūhataḥ samare ripūn
english: "These, blazing in battle with their splendour, swift in flight, are the hero's inexhaustible arrows that scatter enemies in combat."

sanskrit: ye ceme pṛthavo dīrghāś candrabimbārdhadarśanāḥ ete bhīmasya niśitā ripukṣayakarāḥ śarāḥ
english: "And these broad, long arrows that resemble a half-disk of the moon — these are Bhīma's sharp arrows that bring destruction to enemies."

sanskrit: hāridravarṇā ye tv ete hemapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ nakulasya kalāpo 'yaṃ pañcaśārdūlalakṣaṇaḥ
english: "These turmeric-coloured ones with golden nocks, sharpened on stone — this is Nakula's quiver bearing the mark of five tigers."

sanskrit: yenāsau vyajayat kṛtsnāṃ pratīcīṃ diśam āhave kalāpo hy eṣa tasyāsīn mādrīputrasya dhīmataḥ
english: "With which that wise son of Mādrī conquered the entire western quarter in battle — this quiver was his."

sanskrit: ye tv ime bhāskarākārāḥ sarvapāraśavāḥ śarāḥ ete citrāḥ kriyopetāḥ sahadevasya dhīmataḥ
english: "And these arrows shaped like the sun, entirely iron, variegated and furnished with ritual markings — these belong to the wise Sahadeva."

sanskrit: ye tv ime niśitāḥ pītāḥ pṛthavo dīrghavāsasaḥ hemapuṅkhās triparvāṇo rājña ete mahāśarāḥ
english: "And these sharp, yellow, broad, long-shafted great arrows with golden nocks and three nodes — these, O prince, are the king's great arrows."

sanskrit: yas tv ayaṃ sāyako dīrghaḥ śilīpṛṣṭhaḥ śilīmukhaḥ arjunasyaiṣa saṃgrāme gurubhārasaho dṛḍhaḥ
english: "And this long arrow, smooth-backed and sharp-pointed, capable of bearing great weight and firm — this is Arjuna's in battle."
